task: Validate DIG request recovery and lease fencing end to end under realistic coordinator/worker faults

candidates.name: full end-to-end deterministic fault harness
candidates.notes: Exercises WorkerRequestState -> QubesWorkerClient -> framed exchange -> TransactionalWorkerRuntime -> TransactionalMissionStore. Covers lost response after commit, worker/coordinator restart reconciliation, lease reclaim fencing, and 8-worker contention.

candidates.name: component-only unit tests
candidates.notes: Fast and cheap, but misses failures created only by composition across request persistence, transport, runtime, and store boundaries.

candidates.name: real Qubes fault injection immediately
candidates.notes: Highest realism but premature before deterministic semantics are proven; harder to reproduce failures and distinguish transport/policy errors from state-machine defects.

candidates.name: blind retry stress benchmark
candidates.notes: Rejected because retries with fresh identities can duplicate committed mutations and would test the wrong safety contract.

why: Best combined correctness, robustness, and QA coverage while remaining reproducible and cheap enough for every CI run. It validates the exact recovery contract before introducing real Qubes deployment variability.
failuresAndLessons: A transport failure after commit must remain an unknown outcome until request-status reconciliation; it must never be treated as an automatic mutation failure.
Lease expiry and reclaim must fence the stale owner even when the stale complete request has a valid durable requestId.
Concurrency tests should assert unique completed mission IDs, not only a final completed count, to expose duplicate completion paths.
Real Qubes tests remain necessary, but deterministic fault injection should gate them rather than replace them.
safetyScope: Synthetic defensive orchestration only; no real financial transactions, stolen payment data, external exploitation, or security-control weakening.
